newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine says Russia to scrap 20 pct VAT on sugar.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says Russia to scrap 20 pct VAT on sugar.

text.p: Ukrainian Agriculture Minister Mykhailo Zubets said on Thursday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had promised to repeal Moscow's 20 percent value-added tax (VAT) on Ukrainian imported sugar.
Zubets, who also holds the post of deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, also told a news conference that Russia planned to invest heavily in Ukraine's ageing sugar refineries.

"Yeltsin guaranteed he would repeal the recently applied value-added tax of 20 percent," Zubets said. "And the Russian Federation has expressed a desire to have a serious stake in our privatised sugar refineries."

Yeltsin's official visit to Ukraine last week to sign a long-delayed friendship treaty followed meetings by the two country's prime ministers to sign various agreements, including one on economic cooperation.
Relations between the two neighbours has been uneasy since the Soviet Union fell apart six years ago, mainly over the much-disputed Black Sea Fleet, but also over trade matters.
Trade relations are also not as sweet, with Russia accusing Ukraine of flooding its market with cheap refined sugar.
In addition to VAT, Russia also levies a 25 percent import duty on imported Ukrainian sugar.
"We have 192 sugar refineries -- the Russians calculate that they will become co-owners in 170 of them," Zubets said, adding the move would guarantee a market for Ukrainian sugar.

Ukraine announced last year it would begin privatising the refineries, most of which were built in the last century and which Western traders have said are so beyond repair that they should be closed.
Zubets previously announced that as of September 1 Ukraine would take steps to reduce its domestic sugar surplus by limiting the amount of sugar for sale to meet domestic needs of 1.5 million tonnes.
He said the rest of the sugar -- Ukraine produced 3.26 million tonnes last year -- would be sold abroad at world prices.

Ukraine has also traditionally exported to neighbouring Belarus, which started imposing 20 percent import duties on Ukrainian sugar earlier this year, as well as the former Soviet republics of Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan.
